Heliosentrix to approve 7-day burst window and provide a safe list of test routes - customer (Aisha) by 2026-04-12

Aisha Rahman - share list of critical API routes and SLOs for burst test - due 2026-04-12

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-09 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48m
Location: Zoom (recording available)

[00:00] Jordan Meyers: Hey everyone thanks for making time, um this is Jordan from Redwood - AE. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Marisol Vega: Marisol here - CTO, hi all.
[00:09] Kenji Ito: Kenji - Head of ML.
[00:11] Aisha Rahman: Aisha, infra.
[00:13] Evan Cho: Evan SRE.
[00:15] Priya Rao: Priya from Redwood infra team, hey.

[00:22] Jordan Meyers: Cool. Objective for today is short and practical: look at the late March spike, isolate cost drivers, decide whether we need to scale Dedicated pools sooner, and nail down the security artifacts you need for procurement.

[00:38] Marisol Vega: Yeah that spike was the surprise. Our finance team flagged it - 3x token burn in a 48 hour window. We rolled back some traffic but want to understand if it's an outlier or a pattern.

[00:53] Kenji Ito: Technical side - we shipped a prompt change that increased average sequence length, so KV cache hit rate dropped. Also some requests hit longer context windows, so tail latency spiked.

[01:10] Priya Rao: Mm-hmm. If I remember correctly your prefix caching hit rate before was, what, 70 to 75%?
[01:15] Kenji Ito: On stable days yes, around 72%. During the spike dropped to ~28% - our telemetry shows KV cache not being reused.

[01:26] Evan Cho: And from SRE we saw lots of small requests that prevented good batching, so GPUs were underutilized but tokens were wasted, oddly enough.

[01:38] Jordan Meyers: Right, so there's multiple levers - prompt engineering to reduce average context length, batching changes to combine small requests, and possible autoscale config. Priya, can you walk through which knobs we can flip quickly?

[01:53] Priya Rao: Yeah. Two fast wins: enable adaptive batching with a slightly longer wait threshold for non-critical routes - that ups batch size and cuts per-token cost; second, prefix/KV cache tuning, we can extend TTLs and lower cache eviction for those model variants. Both are config flips, low-risk.

[02:12] Aisha Rahman: What's the latency impact of longer batching? Our product goals require 250 ms p50 for chat endpoints.

[02:20] Priya Rao: If you set the adaptive wait to 30 ms we saw p50 increase around 15 to 25 ms in our tests but throughput + cost improved significantly. For users that need strict tail latency we can pin to a lower batching window or route to a low-latency tier.

[02:36] Jordan Meyers: There's also the routing policy - route sensitive traffic to a dedicated low-latency pool (higher cost) and batchable background traffic on optimized shared pools.

[02:47] Marisol Vega: We're evaluating dedicated vs hosted; leadership leans dedicated for predictability but procurement needs SOC2 and on-premish KMS patterns. What does Redwood require for KMS/HSM?

[02:58] Jordan Meyers: We support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations - we have a recommended flow for AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault, and an HSM pattern if you go on-prem. We'll send the checklist.

[03:10] Kenji Ito: Any gotchas on audit logs? We need fine-grained per-request logs for internal compliance.

[03:16] Priya Rao: We capture token-level telemetry and per-request traces in the Console; we can increase retention for enterprise packages and stream audit logs to your SIEM via secure webhook or S3 sink. There's a tiny perf impact at extremely high QPS but it's usually negligible.

[03:33] Aisha Rahman: Good. Procurement also asked about data residency - can Dedicated be pinned to eu-west and restrict egress?

[03:40] Jordan Meyers: Yes, Dedicated pools can be region pinned. For Private we can do VPC peering or an on-prem appliance - network egress controls are part of the package.

[03:50] Evan Cho: Back to the spike, finance asked if we can produce a per-route cost breakdown and a recommended baseline capacity to avoid surprises.

[03:59] Jordan Meyers: We did a quick pass with your token logs - I'll share a per-route sheet. It showed routes /chat/fast and /chat/batch are the heavy hitters. The heavy route had 60% of tokens during the spike.

[04:14] Kenji Ito: The heavy route is the new summarization path used by notifications - it grew unexpectedly after marketing pushed some promotional copy. Classic.

[04:24] Marisol Vega: So tactical: what's the baseline capacity we need for a 3x burst headroom?

[04:30] Priya Rao: Two ways: short term - enable burst capacity on Dedicated and set autoscale to scale up to 3x for 24-72 hours; long term - rightsize model variants and batching so the normal committed capacity covers most spikes. For the short test we propose a 7-day burst window to simulate traffic and measure real cost/latency.

[04:48] Aisha Rahman: That 7-day window sounds fine if we can limit to safe routes. We'll need an explicit kill switch and rollback playbook.

[04:55] Jordan Meyers: Absolutely. We'll provide a runbook with kill switch and preflight checks.

[05:02] Kenji Ito: A couple of nitty gritty items - quantization tolerance: we test Q4-8bit on a shadowed variant, but degrading quality may cause downstream errors. We need to define acceptable failure rates.

[05:13] Priya Rao: For quantization we can run A/B with a small % of traffic and compare scoring on your eval set. If accuracy drops beyond the threshold we fallback to FP16. We also support per-route model pinning so critical flows skip quantized paths.

[05:27] Marisol Vega: Great. What about cost forecasting? Can Redwood provide a rolling 30-day forecast with confidence intervals reflecting current commit + burst options?

[05:36] Jordan Meyers: Yes, the Console provides usage forecasts and a stress-test estimator for burst options. We'll attach a forecast with the 7-day test parameters.

[05:45] Evan Cho: For the test we need to know if enabling extended audit logs will add measurable cost. Also how caching increases affect billing accuracy.

[05:54] Priya Rao: Audit log retention is billed separately if you push to our long-term storage; short-term retention in Console is included. Caching reduces token bills because of cache hits, but you may see more compute for cache management during warmup. Net usually positive.

[06:10] Jordan Meyers: Quick recap of action items - Priya will produce batch/TTL tuning and a simulation; Jordan will send the security pack and pricing; Aisha will share safe route list and approve the 7-day window; Kenji will confirm acceptable accuracy thresholds for quantization.

[06:29] Marisol Vega: Also can you put together a one-page exec summary for our CFO that shows worst case, expected, and recommended commit? They don't want the engineering detail.

[06:37] Jordan Meyers: Yes, we'll do a 1-pager.

[06:40] Kenji Ito: One more thing - any competitors we should watch for in terms of cheaper inference? We saw some tests from Vast.ai but reliability was... questionable.

[06:49] Priya Rao: Vast.ai is spotty; Anthropic and OpenAI are competitors for quality/latency but they're more SaaS-like and can be more costly at scale. We can include a short comparison in the one-pager.

[06:59] Aisha Rahman: Ok wrapping. Quick timelines: Jordan security pack by tomorrow, Aisha safe routes by Monday, Priya tuning doc by next Thursday.

[07:12] Jordan Meyers: Perfect. We'll follow up in the thread with the runbook and a calendar invite for the 7-day burst start. Thanks all.

[07:20] Meeting end.
